_comment: FULL STACK — per-worktree containers behind an nginx sub-path, plus an
isolated database copy. The heaviest option and the most complete: each
well as on its own port.
Only use this when docker-compose.yml is NOT tracked in git: create-worktree
generates one in the worktree and would overwrite a committed file.
PREREQUISITE: a .env in the main checkout. It is both the source of the
database credentials and the env_file the generated compose service reads.
docker.network_default is the network the main stack already runs on — the
worktree's containers join it so they can reach Postgres by service name.
network_pattern is the fallback lookup when that exact name is absent.
nginx.config is a file included by your local nginx; it needs a line reading
'# END WORKTREE ROUTES' inside the server block, which is where route blocks
are inserted. Without that marker nothing is written and the script says so.
worker describes a background queue container: 'none' for web-only. The
queue_env var is rewritten per worktree so jobs don't cross branches.
